Hi Tom & Priya,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier this week — excited about the Syzygy Tools + Redwood alliance. We agreed the next step is a short technical validation to confirm an efficient reference deployment and a sandbox run to exercise end-to-end inference (hosted Redwood API -> Syzygy pre/post-processing hooks).

To keep this focused, can you confirm the following so our engineering team can prepare a validation harness:
- Primary model families you expect to serve (LLM family / quantization expectations).
- Typical max sequence lengths and concurrency profile for your expected pipelines.
- Whether you need prefix/KV cache passthrough or plan to manage cache client-side.
- Network / egress constraints for sandboxes (we can provide a temporary VPC peering).

I attached a lightweight reference architecture PDF (redwood-ref-arch-syzygy-v1.pdf) that shows two candidate flows (direct API + pre-processing sidecar). Please skim and flag any immediate redlines.

Proposed plan:
- You share sandbox creds + network matrix -> Redwood validates connectivity and a quick smoke run.
- Redwood runs a 2-hour lab exercising batching, caching, and token-cost profiling.
- We share a short readout and recommended configuration for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Can you confirm sandbox timeline this week or early next?

Thanks,

Kimberly — thanks for the clear plan and the reference doc. Priya and I synced and we can get a sandbox spun up, but a couple of quick clarifications so we configure the right environment: 

1) Model & quantization: we intend to evaluate two families — a T5-derived seq2seq (float16 / int8 quant option) and a Llama-like decoder (int8). Our internal preprocessing attaches metadata tokens; ideally we avoid re-tokenizing on Redwood side.

2) Sequence lengths: typical payloads are 512 tokens, but we sometimes see bursts to 2k for document-level jobs; concurrency per tenant is modest (5–20 concurrent requests) but parallel across many tenants.

3) Cache: we can support client-side KV cache for the document-level flows, but for the short-chat path we prefer Redwood-managed prefix caching to reduce latency.

4) Sandbox access: we have a staging VPC and can peer. We'll need a short list of IP ranges for the smoke test and an SSH jump host for debug logs. 

I'll attach our sandbox network matrix and a sample anonymized request/response pair. Once we get the IP list and a contact for sandbox creds, we'll provision overnight.

Tom

Quick technical readout based on Tom's notes and an initial pass on the ref architecture: 

- Quantization: Our runtime supports int8 for decoder-only families and int8/float16 hybrid paths for encoder-decoder (T5) with model-specific kernel selection. No repackaging required for standard int8 conversions; we'll validate a sample model in the sandbox. 

- Prefix cache passthrough: Redwood currently exposes prefix cache hooks in the 2026-11 API (opt-in header x-rw-prefix-cache). For Syzygy's chat path we can enable passthrough without infra changes — will need to document header semantics for their pre-processing sidecar.

- Sequence lengths & batching: 2k bursts will push memory on the smaller GPU profiles. Proposed lab config: one p4d-like node for mixed workloads with continuous batching disabled during burst windows (to preserve latency). We'll run 10 runs at 5–20 concurrent clients to capture latency tail.

- Networking: we can accept a peered VPC or a restricted IP list. For debug we prefer an ephemeral SSH jump host behind our firewall; we'll rotate creds post-test.

Actionables I took:
- Created lab slot Wed 2026-12-02 09:00–11:00 PT and added Marissa as owner.
- Spun up a staging model instance for an int8 decoder sample (logs will be in shared drive).
- Drafted a short runbook for the smoke tests (link in RH).

I'll attach a checklist and the minimal kernel/ops questions we might ask Syzygy if their sample model uses custom ops. If they do, that's a potential blocker until we get buildable kernels.

Sergio
